items.title: 68163_Tom Whaley oral history interview
items.q: in 1919 Fletcher Henderson came to Boston and he was the greatest band in the world there... He had Louie Armstrong in the band... I used to tell the fellows you got to learn to read that music, because Fletcher Henderson had one of the greatest bands

ctx.x: No, not Joe Turner. He had a band, he's got a lady that sings with him now in his band and he left here in 1920 something and went to Europe. He's one of the first bands I think that went to Russia. I am trying to think of his name. Can you recall his name.

No, I don't. Well, I tell you, in 1919 Fletcher Henderson came to Boston and he was the greatest band in the world there, because he could play waltzes, and that's the Massachusetts -- what's the name of the hall up there. Horicultural Hall was crowded, people would come there to hear Fletcher Henderson play waltzes. He had Louie Armstrong in the band, he had Don Redman , oh, he had a whole -- what's the clarinet player. Buster Bailey. He had all them people and he could arrange and he used to arrange for the…
player, the fellow now, Benny Goodman. Sure.
